payload.name: Extract Explicit Resource Suggestions
payload.description: When a message contains an explicit suggestion or recommendation from one speaker to another to check out a specific resource (e.g., a book, article, website) for insights on a topic, extract it as a candidate event memory during construction.
content: During extraction, if any message explicitly recommends or suggests that the main user (or another named speaker) consult a specific, named resource (book, article, website, video, etc.) for insights on a topic, create a candidate event memory capturing: who made the suggestion, to whom, the resource mentioned, and the topic it addresses.

Do not skip such candidates merely because the recommended resource appears only as advice, because the message is from a speaker other than the main user, or because the topic (e.g., a dream) is personal.

Stop after one candidate per suggestion; do not expand to every noun or mentioned item. If no concrete resource is named, or the message only asks for a recommendation without making one, no candidate is needed.

solves: The general failure is that explicit suggestions of concrete resources are missed during extraction, so later questions about who recommended what cannot be answered. This Skill applies when a speaker explicitly tells another to check out a named resource for insights on a topic. It does not apply when no concrete resource is named or when the message merely asks for a recommendation.
